Create function to Efficiently compute distances from one tree to others in a set

Source: R/DistanceOracle.R
DistanceOracle.Rd

DistanceOracle() prepares a set of trees and returns a function that efficiently computes the distances from any one of them to all of them.

Usage

DistanceOracle(trees, Func = ClusteringInfoDistance, ..., maxBytes = 2^31)

Arguments

trees

List of trees of class phylo or Splits, or a multiPhylo object.

Func

Function giving the distance between trees: one of ClusteringInfoDistance(), InfoRobinsonFoulds(), RobinsonFoulds(), MatchingSplitDistance(), NyeSimilarity() (returns a similarity unless similarity = FALSE), or JaccardRobinsonFoulds().

...

Further arguments to Func, such as normalize.

maxBytes

Numeric giving the maximum memory, in bytes, that the prepared trees may occupy.

Value

DistanceOracle() returns a function that takes a single argument i, an integer vector that specifies the indices of one or more elements in trees. That function returns the values of Func between trees[[i]] and each tree in trees: a vector if i has length one, otherwise a matrix with one column per entry of i.

Details

In use cases that require one column of a distance matrix at a time, it is faster to run a single preparation pass over all trees, than to repeat the preparatory steps each time a new column is required. DistanceOracle() produces a function that, when passed i, returns the same as Func(trees[[i]], trees, ...); repeated calls to that function are faster than repeated calls to Func.

Columns are computed using getOption("mc.cores") threads.

See also

Other tree distances: HierarchicalMutualInfo(), JaccardRobinsonFoulds(), KendallColijn(), MASTSize(), MatchingSplitDistance(), NNIDist(), NNIMaxStep(), NyeSimilarity(), PathDist(), Robinson-Foulds, SPRDist(), TransferDist(), TreeDistance()

Author

Martin R. Smith (martin.smith@durham.ac.uk)

Examples

library("TreeTools", quietly = TRUE)
trees <- as.phylo(0:9, nTip = 12)
Oracle <- DistanceOracle(trees, ClusteringInfoDistance)
Oracle(3)
#>  [1] 1.114993 1.114993 0.000000 2.417249 2.417249 1.375291 1.735396 2.329028
#>  [9] 1.995695 2.329028
all.equal(Oracle(3), ClusteringInfoDistance(trees[[3]], trees))
#> [1] TRUE
